title: A cloudflare-sandbox executor that returns a handle, not a result
description:
internal/exec/ implements herdr and subprocess. runstate.Executors already reserves the NAME 'cloudflare-sandbox' with nothing behind it. This tick is the implementation, and it is the Go client of the route 8ty exposes.

The shape that matters, and it is yoh's principle rather than a preference: the executor returns a HANDLE, not a finished attempt. It starts work in a sandbox and comes back. Something else asks later whether that handle is done. An executor that blocks until an attempt finishes puts a wall clock inside a dispatch and is the thing 'nothing waits' exists to forbid.

t5p already persisted the sandbox handle so an attempt survives a Workflow restart, which suggests the durable half of this is in place - read it before designing a new one.

Check internal/runconfig/kinds.go for what a runner kind is required to supply, and internal/exec/subprocess for the interface the local executor satisfies, because this one satisfies the same interface with a different substrate. Where the interface assumes a local process (signals, stdio, exit codes), the assumption IS the work - name each one you had to reinterpret in the tick's report rather than silently papering over it.
acceptance_criteria: internal/exec gains a cloudflare-sandbox executor that satisfies the same interface as subprocess, starts an attempt through the Worker route and returns a handle without blocking, a handle can be re-queried for state after the process that created it is gone, and go test -short ./... passes
